pointers.sentence: `AdminSite.disable_action` takes a name from the enabled ones, `AdminSite.actions`, but not from the dictionary `AdminSite.get_action` reads, so a disabled action named in one model admin's `ModelAdmin.actions` comes back for that one (`django/contrib/admin/sites.py:AdminSite.disable_action`).
A method comes from the class, unbound, so that, as the comment says, methods and functions are called alike, with the model admin first (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.get_action`).

`ModelAdmin._get_base_actions` puts the site's enabled actions first, less those the model admin's list names, then the model admin's, keeping those located on the page being built (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin._get_base_actions`).

Each is an `Action`, a dataclass of the function, its name, its description, its plural description and its locations (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:Action`), read from attributes that the decorator `django.contrib.admin.action` sets on the function: `"short_description"`, `"plural_description"` (the description when no plural is given) and `"locations"`, where one `ActionLocation` is made a list; the `"allowed_permissions"` it sets too are not copied into the `Action` (`django/contrib/admin/decorators.py:action`).

Each is an `Action`, a dataclass of the function, its name, its description, its plural description and its locations (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:Action`), read from attributes that the decorator `django.contrib.admin.action` sets on the function: `"short_description"`, `"plural_description"` (the description when no plural is given) and `"locations"`, where one `ActionLocation` is made a list; the `"allowed_permissions"` it sets too are not copied into the `Action` (`django/contrib/admin/decorators.py:action`).

Otherwise `ModelAdmin._filter_actions_by_permissions` keeps an action without `"allowed_permissions"`, and one with them when any of the model admin's methods they name is true for the request: `"change"` names `BaseModelAdmin.has_change_permission`, asked without an object even on a change form (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin._filter_actions_by_permissions`).

`ModelAdmin.get_action_choices` makes the action form's choices: a blank one, then each name with a description formatted with the model's verbose names: the plural description on the change list, the description on a change form (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.get_action_choices`).

The change list shows an `ActionForm`, a choice field `"action"` and a hidden boolean `"select_across"`, which the page's JavaScript sets when the user selects every row the change list matches (`django/contrib/admin/helpers.py:ActionForm`).

The action form may stand above and below the list (`ModelAdmin.actions_on_top`, `ModelAdmin.actions_on_bottom`), both inside the form that holds the list, and each copy's Run button posts `"index"`, the copy's number (`django/contrib/admin/templatetags/admin_list.py:admin_actions`).

`ModelAdmin.changelist_view` calls `response_action` from two places, each for a `"POST"` to a model admin with actions and without `"_save"`, the save button of `ModelAdmin.list_editable` ([The change list's columns: `list_display` and `list_editable`](list-display.md)) (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.changelist_view`).

`delete_selected` is declared with `django.contrib.admin.action` as asking for `"delete"`, and described as "Delete selected %(verbose_name_plural)s" (`django/contrib/admin/actions.py:delete_selected`).

Otherwise it is titled "Delete multiple objects", lists the objects, and holds a form of hidden inputs: each key as `"_selected_action"`, `"action"` as `"delete_selected"`, and `"post"` as `"yes"` (`django/contrib/admin/templates/admin/delete_selected_confirmation.html`).

`delete_queryset` calls `QuerySet.delete`, for efficiency, the documentation says, so `Model.delete` is not called ([Creating, updating and deleting through a queryset](../querysets/writing.md)) (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.delete_queryset`, `docs/ref/contrib/admin/actions.txt`).

`ModelAdmin._changeform_view` asks `get_actions` for `ActionLocation.CHANGE_FORM` and, on a change page with any, makes the action form with the prefix `"CHANGE_FORM"` (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin._changeform_view`).

Since 6.1, unpacking or indexing an `Action` like the tuple it replaced warns with `RemovedInDjango2028Warning`, as, through `warn_about_implementation`, does overriding `get_actions` or `get_action_choices` without `action_location=`; such a `get_actions` gives a change form no actions (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin._get_actions_with_action_location`) ([Deprecation: warnings named by year, `warn_about_external_use` and `deprecate_posargs`](../utils/deprecation.md)).
